key_insight: Explainable deep reinforcement learning can optimize building energy management while making the controller’s decisions more transparent and trustworthy.
engineering_relevance: For PV-equipped buildings with storage, tariffs, and heat pumps, this approach can reduce electricity cost and improve operational control using data-driven policies that are easier to interpret.
method: Train on-policy and off-policy DRL agents for residential energy scheduling
Use an expanded state space with demand, PV output, battery state, weather, prices, forecasts, and calendar/holiday signals
Apply post-hoc explainability methods to interpret learned control policies
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate both synthetic data and real-world LLEC at KIT data and report that A2C and PPO outperform off-policy methods in cumulative reward and policy stability.
watch_item: Results depend on forecast quality and real-world deployment robustness; explainability does not eliminate the need for careful validation under changing building conditions.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
